title: A Sharp Local-Question Threshold for GHZ-Equatorial Completeness in Four-Player XOR Games
authors: Ziao Tang, Chengkai Zhu, Ge Bai, Xin Wang, Ranyiliu Chen
abstract: We determine the smallest number of active questions per player at which a four-player binary exclusive-or (XOR) game of commuting-operator value one need not admit a Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger (GHZ) equatorial realization. Such a realization uses the four-qubit GHZ state and equatorial qubit observables, reducing perfect play to additive phase equations. We prove that every four-player XOR game with commuting-operator value one and at most three active questions per player has a perfect GHZ-equatorial strategy. Conversely, we construct a uniform eight-clause game with four active questions per player whose commuting-operator value is one but whose phase equations are inconsistent. Thus four is the sharp local-question threshold. The positive result follows by lifting every integral incidence obstruction to an ordered noncommutative refutation, using primitive circuits, forest matchings, and ternary Hamming geometry. For the separating game, a Klein four-group incidence relation obstructs the phase system, while an even-subgroup normal form and degree-one and degree-two Magnus coefficients exclude refutations of arbitrary length.
summary: This theoretical paper establishes a sharp boundary (threshold) for four-player XOR games concerning the equivalence between two models of quantum correlation: those defined by commuting operators and those admitting perfect Greenberger–Horne–Zeilinger (GHZ)-equatorial strategies. The authors prove that this threshold is exactly four active questions per player, using advanced algebraic geometry and formal proof techniques.
main_problem: The paper determines the sharp local-question threshold for when a four-player XOR game's commuting-operator value ($\omega_{co}(G)=1$) guarantees a perfect Greenberger–Horne–Zeilinger (GHZ)-equatorial realization.
main_result: Four is established as the sharp threshold: games with $\le 3$ questions per player must have a perfect GHZ-equatorial strategy if $\omega_{co}(G)=1$, but this fails for some game with four questions per player.
method: The analysis reduces the problem to analyzing phase equations derived from the GHZ state and uses advanced mathematical tools like primitive circuits, forest matchings, and ternary Hamming geometry to prove algebraic equivalences between different correlation models.
model_or_system: The model is a four-player binary XOR game defined by clauses and questions. The analysis compares correlations achievable via tensor-product strategies versus those constrained by commuting operators on a single Hilbert space (GHZ state).
key_observables: Commuting-operator value ($\omega_{co}(G)$), perfect MERP strategy existence, and the phase equations derived from the GHZ state.
important_parameters: The number of active questions per player ($k$), specifically testing $k=3$ versus $k=4$.
main_assumptions: The proof relies on lifting abelian obstructions to ordered non-commutative refutations and utilizes formal verification in Lean 4.30.0.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows the core dependency graph for the Lean formalization, mapping theorems to their ingredients; Table 2 provides a statement-by-statement correspondence between manuscript results and Lean declarations.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by establishing algebraic dualities relating perfect strategies ($\omega_{co}(G)=1$) to lattice conditions ($b \in L^{\perp}_E$ vs $b \in R^{\perp}_E$). It then uses geometric arguments (e.g., covering the cube with balls) and graph theory/algebraic techniques (Cayley matching classification) to prove the threshold result.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous, mathematically deep characterization of when non-local quantum correlations implied by specific game structures can be perfectly simulated using only local measurements on a highly entangled state like the GHZ state.
